newsitem.title: UK: Aston Villa shares yo-yo on debut day.
newsitem.headline: Aston Villa shares yo-yo on debut day.

text.p: Former European football champions Aston Villa made a topsy-turvy debut on the London Stock Exchange on Wednesday as the English soccer season draws towards its close with many soccer clubs shares languishing near their year lows.

Villa came to the market with a price tag of around 125 million pounds ($205 million) making it the fourth biggest British soccer club in terms of market capitalisation behind English champions Manchester United, Newcastle United and Chelsea Village.
Analysts said the stock was nearly fully valued at the issue price but suggested there was investor interest in the shares as it soon rose to a premium.
The shares, issued at 11 pounds peaked at 12 pounds before sliding back to 10.75 in late trade. Dealers said the afternoon slide was a result of investors taking profits.
Nick Batram, share analyst at brokers Greig Middleton, saw the general fall in soccer club shares from their highs in the first two months of the year as a "healthy set-back."
"I think we will see some evaluation of the individual clubs over the summer months while investors are less sidetracked by the teams' results," said Batram.
"We could see the better quality stocks building a solid base at these levels," he said.
Southampton and Sunderland are typical of shares hit by on-field performances as both clubs have been embroiled in the premier league relegation battle.

Southampton's shares have dropped from their year high of 158p on January 15 but have recovered from the their year low of 73p as they look like avoiding relegation with one match to go. On Wednesday, the shares were trading at 103-1/2p.

Less certain of a place in the premier league next season are Sunderland who face the unappetising task of having to beat Wimbledon on their homeground Sunday to escape demotion. Sunderland's shares stood at 475p, a fall of almost three pounds from their year high of 765p.

Shares in Chelsea Village Plc , owner of Chelsea FC, continued to trade just above their low of 114-1/2p in spite of a place in the FA Cup final and the prospect of a lucrative place in Europe next season.
Chelsea's shares on Wednesday were up 7-1/2p to 127-1/2p but well off the year's high of 170p set on February 7.
"Chelsea have issued an enormous amount of stock this year and I think the market is suffering from indigestion," said Batram.

Newcastle United's shares have fallen almost continually since floating on the stock market at 135p on April 2. The north-east club's share price has dropped from 155p on the first day of dealings as the team has failed to win any silverware.
The shares have recaptured some form to 119p , up from their year low of 114p set on April 22, as Newcastle have qualified to play in the UEFA Cup next season.

Shares in newly crowned Premier League champions, Manchester United have failed to break out of a narrow three month trading range even though the UK's largest soccer club have won the title for the fourth time in five years.
Since February 13, the shares have traded between a high of 678p and low of 625p and were down 19p on Wednesday at 642p, the day after lifting the league championship trophy.
